## What it is

The flat-printing twin-rail overhead boom. Print one.

## Design notes

The 177 mm reach is measured from the mast/socket centerline and places the selected rear camera over the center of a portrait reMarkable 2. A twin-rail rectangle resists torsion better than a single arm. Two 24.2 x 18.2 mm collars provide 14 mm of mast engagement and stop against the solid boom beam. Inside each collar, two integral 5.2 mm dowels engage 12 mm into the existing mast-end pin sockets. The collars and dowels print upward without support; flip the boom over during assembly so they face down. The 6.4 mm hole carries the printed tool-free cradle locking pin.

Four sub-1 mm² faces are the expected corner triangles where the 1 mm polish chamfers meet on the two socket collars.

## Don't

Do not remove the integral alignment dowels: without them, the boom merely rests on the mast collars while the visible mast-end holes do nothing. Do not restore the original through-sockets: they had no depth stop and could slide down the masts. Do not restore the original 24.4 x 18.4 mm mast clearance; it physically wobbled in the base. Do not replace this with one centered cantilever: it twists under off-axis camera weight. Do not add structure along the tablet sides.
